title: Union 802 hiring floor and prejudice in music
summary: Sam says only white names are called for gigs on the union floor and that prejudice exists everywhere.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: It is, it actually is, man. I don't care what you say, man. In music there is racial; there is prejudice. It's racial, it's anything you want to call it, in music, man. Now they say there is no room for it. And I can go along with that, sure. There is no room for prejudice when you're playing music man. But man, you go around to 802 and stand there, just stand down there for about 15 - what days, get music, start calling musicians?
One of those days, down on the floor, yes.
And all you can hear is Weinstein. You can't hear no Mitchells and Jones and Smiths and Johnsons. They don't have none of them.
And you see all white dudes they are calling down there for gigs, not one black dude nowhere they'll be calling,

you see. Now I detected that years ago. I used to talk about that man and guys would look at me. I used to talk about that to white musicians man and guys would look at me funny, you know as if I'd better keep cool. You better keep cool, you won't be gigging.
Yeah, that's the thing I always resented too, that they'd want to dress that thing. You're supposed to feel a draft.

You're supposed to feel a draft. But you see they don't talk with you about that. A few of those guys. And I mentioned it, I make it my business to every white guy and dude that I work with, you know you don't work with too many of them but especially when you're playing with a duo, I drop it on the scene, man. "Do they ever call you down at the union when they'd be calling the musicians for a gig?" "No." I say "they don't ever call me either, why? I wonder why." Start a conversation that way.
They don't want to talk with you about that. They change the subject right quick, you know.

So don't ever let anybody fool you, man. There is prejudice man, prejudice in music, man, and not only around here, it's all over the world. And I see it over in Europe too, where a lot of the musicians are going back and
